one_liner: orlp/ed25519 compiled to a size-optimized WebAssembly module; about 10x faster than pure-JS @noble/curves 0.7.0 for Ed25519.
what_it_does: An npm package that exposes Ed25519 key generation, signing and verification from orlp/ed25519 (pinned to commit 7fa6712e) through an Emscripten-built WebAssembly module, with the same API as supercop.js but Uint8Array instead of Buffer. You call supercop.ready(cb) once, then createSeed, createKeyPair(seed), sign(msg, publicKey, secretKey) and verify(sig, msg, publicKey); it runs in Node and modern browsers (UMD/AMD/CommonJS). It is not a drop-in for node:crypto KeyObjects or for NaCl-style 64-byte secret keys.
how_it_is_fast: The speed comes from running the ref10-derived C field and group arithmetic of orlp/ed25519 (radix-2^25.5 field elements, precomputed base-point tables for ge_scalarmult_base) as WebAssembly instead of JavaScript BigInt or number arithmetic. The JS wrapper only copies inputs into the wasm heap with malloc, calls the exported C function and copies the result out. The build is tuned for size (-Oz, LTO, Closure), not speed.
when_to_use: Browser or Node code that needs Ed25519 sign/verify on raw key bytes and is currently on an old pure-JS library such as @noble/curves 0.7.x or supercop.js
Bundles where module size matters: the wasm build is size-optimized and the README says it is multiple times smaller than supercop.js
Workloads that already store keys as raw bytes, where node:crypto would need a KeyObject import per call (the serialized node:crypto row was about 3x slower in the berith table)
Projects already using the supercop.js API that want a faster, smaller replacement with the same key format
when_not_to_use: Node with KeyObject-held keys: native node:crypto measured 152.67 vs 187.96 us per keygen+sign+verify in the same table

Interoperating with libsodium, tweetnacl or RFC 8032 seed-based keys: the 64-byte secretKey is the clamped SHA-512 expansion of the seed, not seed||publicKey, so secret keys are not interchangeable (orlp/ed25519 issue #35)

Consensus or strict-verification settings: verify only rejects signatures whose top three bits of S are set, it does not check S < L or reject small-order or non-canonical public keys, so it accepts malleable signatures that strict verifiers reject
Code that needs maintenance, audits or side-channel guarantees: last commit and npm release 5.0.1 date from 2018-02-24, with no constant-time claim in the README
Signing very large messages in one call: the build does not set ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH, so the message must fit in Emscripten's fixed default heap (limit not documented)

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (prebuilt src/supercop.js and wasm in the npm package); rebuilding needs Emscripten, gulp and LiveScript plus a vendored orlp/ed25519 checkout
integration.min_toolchain: Any engine with WebAssembly support (Node 8+ era, modern browsers); Emscripten version used for the published build is not documented
integration.platforms: any WebAssembly host (Node, browsers); no SIMD or threads
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each module instance keeps a shared list of allocated pointers in JS, so use one instance per thread or worker
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same operations as @noble/curves ed25519 but a different API (ready callback, seed-to-keypair, sign takes the public key) and an incompatible 64-byte secret-key format

gotchas: sign(msg, publicKey, secretKey) trusts the caller's publicKey: the nonce depends only on the secret key and message, so signing the same message under two different public keys yields two signatures with the same R and lets an attacker recover the private scalar; always pass the matching key.
Secret keys and messages are copied into the wasm heap and released with free() without being zeroed, so key material can remain in linear memory after a call.

Benchmark harness: the berith bench at HEAD (src/node/bench/index.bench.ts) has no serialized node:crypto row, so the 555.61 us figure came from an older harness version; every iteration mixes RNG, keygen, sign and verify of a 1,024-byte message, and the verify result is never checked.
The published wasm is built with -Oz (size first); a speed-optimized build of the same C would likely be faster, but no such number is published.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other Ed25519 or signature library is catalogued in this category; hash-wasm is the closest wasm crypto sibling but covers hashes only, so pick supercop.wasm when you need signatures in JS and can accept an old, unaudited code base.
verified_claims_summary: In a third-party benchmark in the competing hazae41/berith repo (Node v18.12.1, Apple M1 Max, 1,000 samples of keygen + sign + verify on a 1,024-byte message), supercop.wasm 5.0.1 took 187.96 us per iteration against 1.99 ms for pure-JS @noble/curves 0.7.0 (about 10.6x, derived from page data); native node:crypto was faster at 152.67 us with KeyObject keys and slower at 555.61 us when keys were serialized.
status_note: Abandoned since 2018-02-24 (34 commits, 13 stars, one enhancement issue) but 0BSD-licensed and tiny, so it can be vendored; treat it as legacy code because of the orlp key format, lax verification and absent maintenance.
